T2.5: fix the pilot go/no-go rule before running it

P2e sections 1.3 and 11 require this ahead of any result, because the pilot is
the step most exposed to expectation. Written against the positioning rather
than a metric, since the positioning is what a negative result would force us to
rewrite.

GO if SNI-D is within 0.02 AUROC of the best post-hoc comparator or the paired
Wilcoxon over 15 (regime, seed) cells is not significant. CONDITIONAL GO if it
loses but costs <=50% and needs no downstream model -- the claim then shrinks to
a free, model-free first-order audit signal. NO-GO otherwise. Independent NO-GO
if SNI-D's median cross-seed Spearman is below 0.5, since a tool an order of
magnitude less stable than its own published 0.951 is not the tool the paper
describes.

Axis A uses main-experiment hyperparameters, fixing B18: R0's synthetic run used
epochs 50 / heads 4 / emb 32, so its "Prior-Only wins" result may be
under-training. Agreement with SHAP is explicitly not a target -- B13 measured
rho = -0.357 there.

T2d.1: fix the decision rule before measuring

P2d section 8 requires the rule to be committed ahead of any result, because
"should SNI stay on the GPU" has already been answered wrongly once (P2c 4.1,
withdrawn as B81).

Three conditions, all required: CPU cost <= 3x CUDA per dataset (not on the
mean); per-cell cost at 12-way concurrency <= 1.5x solo, counting only batches
where every job finished; CPU/GPU metric difference no larger than the same
metric's cross-seed spread, with an absolute 1e-3 fallback so a degenerate
denominator cannot make the condition unfalsifiable.

The CUDA side is reused from the P2c smoke arm, which ran exactly this
configuration. The void SNI/AutoMPG timing is excluded.
